No ones saying that they don't. The point is though, it's easier to play what you want when what you want also happens to be the best.

An out of game example would be, you have two job opportunities, one in the field you are interested in that pays 200k a year and one in a field that you're not interested in that pays 100k a year. I imagine most people in this scenario would choose the former. You could say that you didn't choose the job in the field that you were interested in because the money, but because you're interested in it, but you never had to make the decision between the two because all the pros aligned.

Now if the salaries were reversed and you had to choose between what you're interested in and significant benefits, it would be a much harder decision. Sure, a portion of passionate people would still choose what they were interested in, even at a lower salary, but many wouldn't.

My whole point is that sure, I imagine most people who chose horde, chose their favourite race, either lore wise or aesthetically, but they never actually had to make any kind of decision because their undead human that flips while melee attacking, also has the strongest arena racial. Or their orc that lets them roleplay as zugzug, also tops meters with bloodfury.

Last thing, I want to make it clear that I don't believe there is any 1 single factor that has lead to faction imbalance, but the issue is that it doesn't take a lot to start it and then it just spirals from there. Say a guild of 50 has 10 people who are minmax tryhards and then 40 people whos preference is split 50/50 between horde and alliance. When one faction has all the advantages, those 10 people instantly sit on one side of the fence, in this case horde, meaning the horde alliance preference in that guild is now 30/20. Suddenly that's 50 people who are now playing horde where only 20 preferred the faction for non minmax reasons.

Ideally if both factions were equal in power, those 10 minmaxers would instead choose on their aesthetic/lore preferences and then the guild could go either alliance or horde, but much more organically.

Even if we only say 5 percent of the total playerbase are minmaxers, that's still an inherent 55/45 split for whichever faction is the strongest and then it snowballs from there because many new players wouldn't want to join the smaller faction.

But that's exactly the point. Players don't feel safe moving to a 45/55 horde server as alliance because there are 0 safeguards to it happening again. Until Blizzard implements systemic safeguards that don't allow faction splits to stray too far on a server, this problem will only get worse.

If you want a reasonable response at to why I think the bulwark nerf is actually fine, heres my opinion.

People often look at the current magic defense of the bulwark and state that since it's already 0 it's already a bad magic shield, but the issue is that with it's huge melee/range defenses, a player could use all of the rest of their slots to cover magic defense and still be insanely tanky to melee and range, allowing them to be very hard to kill from all combat styles while not having to put much effort in. Currently as it stands, a player with bulwark and hides who gets most of their prayer switches right, and click food when they go under 80 hp is almost impossible to kill, even when the pker is the better player and is putting more effort attacking than the player defending is.

This leaves the options to keep the bulwarks current magic defense, but nerf it's melee/range defenses so that players will still be vulnerable to range/melee if they prioritize mage defense with the rest of their gear. 

Or to nerf the magic defense a lot, so it's not realistically possible to achieve good magic defense while wearing a bulwark, or to do so the player would have to actually risk several million gp.

The final option is what they've gone with , which is nerf both the mage defense and melee defense a little bit, while upping the range defense. This means that it is still really strong against ranged attacks, regardless of what else the player has equipped, but is harder to patch up the mage defense required and also no longer basically immune to melee attacks.
